messages:
Maya: FYI noticed a jump in p99 for small requests after yesterday's kernel selector change. p50 stable but p99 +40ms. Anyone else see this?
Jon: saw that in the dashboards too. p99 spikes coincide with tail microbursts. Screenshot: https://grafana/redwood/d/abc
Priya: I profiled a 128-token request that hit the slow path. KV cache lookups seemed fine but kernel fallback triggered for ~12% of calls. Dumped trace attached.
Maya: can you paste the light trace here?
Priya: sure
Priya: ```
# trace snippet
request_id=xyz
kernel_chosen=quant_opt_fallback
kernel_latency_ms=22
kv_hit=true
extended_wait_ms=9
```
Kevin: interesting — fallback latency ~22ms vs fast kernel ~6ms. That alone explains p99 delta. Why is fallback happening for short sequences?
Li: my hunch: the kernel selection threshold uses estimated batch token size. Microbatches with weird token distributions push selection to fallback. We adjusted threshold to prefer fallback for safety in last change.
Jon: right — change was `kernel_choice: prefer_stable_when_batch_tokens>2048` -> we lowered threshold to 1536 to avoid a rare OOM. Might be too aggressive.
Maya: so two levers: revert threshold or tweak scheduler to reduce chance of hitting those conditions (reduce max_batch_tokens or lower max_wait_ms to reduce microbatch growth).
Priya: ran an experiment: reduced `max_batch_tokens` from 4096->3072 and `max_wait_ms` 12->6 for a subset pool. Observed p99 drop ~18ms but overall throughput -5%. Tail shape improved though.
SREBot: deploy job #deploy-314 started for canary group eng-runtime-canary-7
Kevin: good to know. Also KV priming: we saw ~3% of requests getting cold KV due to coalescing delays; that amplifies fallback effects. Suggest enabling eager-KV-priming for small seqs in the pool.
Li: can we simulate kernel-choice decision probability? I wrote a quick sampler that replays request length distributions with scheduler params. Output: fallback_rate@1536thr=11.8%, @2048thr=7.2% for same traffic.
Maya: thanks. How about p99 impact estimate?
Li: approximate: p99 = base_p99 + fallback_rate * (fallback_latency - fast_latency). Using base_p99 10ms, fallback 22ms, fast 6ms -> at 11.8% p99 ~ 10 + .118*(16) = 11.9ms (but real world shows bigger due to KV cold).
Priya: I pushed a flamegraph to the canary logs. Link: https://perf/redwood/flame/314
Jon: action plan proposal: 1) revert kernel threshold change in canary for 24h 2) apply `max_wait_ms=6` for microburst-sensitive pools 3) enable eager-KV-priming for seq<=64 4) collect p95/p99 and CPU/GPU utilization
Maya: agree. Also add a short A/B to measure throughput delta over 1% traffic. If throughput loss >7% we rollback.
Kevin: I'll own the config patch and rollout. Will annotate with ticket #RINF-4921.
SREBot: deploy #deploy-314 succeeded on 6/6 canary hosts :tada:
Priya: initial canary numbers look good: p99 down ~20ms, throughput -3% so far.
Jon: thanks. Follow-up: let's run a kernel chooser unit test that emits the decision reason into traces so we can correlate selection with queue sizes in future.
Maya: +1. Also add a perf regression alert on any p99 increase >10ms vs baseline for the pool.
Li: I'll add the sampler to repo under `tools/scheduling/` and a small README with reproduction steps.
Maya: great, thx all. We'll reconvene if canary changes diverge after 2h.
